problems.title: The documented six-stack resident-weight configuration lacks capacity
problems.source_location: Latest arXiv v1, Sections 4.1/5.1/5.2 and Tables 1–2, PDF pp. 6–8
claim: The setup lists \(30.5\) billion parameters, FP16 weights and six HBM2 stacks of \(8192\) MB, with distributed resident weight storage.
analysis: One FP16 copy needs \(30.5\times10^9\cdot2=61\times10^9\) bytes. Even treating each listed stack as \(8192\) MiB gives only \(48\) GiB \(=51539607552\) bytes, a shortfall of \(9460392448\) bytes. Assigning all \(17\cdot100\) tiles' \(2.265\) MiB SRAM to weights still gives only about \(55.577\) GB. A smaller per-token active parameter count does not store the remaining experts; another memory/offload/compression layer could, but must be identified.
result: The documented resident-weight interpretation is inconsistent by capacity arithmetic. Host/offload/extra-stack traces could resolve it; the source does not establish that no such unreported mechanism exists. Simulator throughput and energy values were not independently recomputed.
assumptions: The finding concerns the stated source version and mathematical or released-code scope.
repair: Provide the actual memory hierarchy and trace. Added storage, offload or compression changes the capacity/performance model and requires explicit evaluation.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: The later arXiv version, posted in March 2026, retains the six-stack FP16 configuration and the listed capacities. The current author repository README provides no additional memory hierarchy or simulator trace resolving this arithmetic.

problems.title: Tightness of a general upper bound depends on the layout quantifier
problems.source_location: Latest arXiv v1, token-copy upper bound and expert/attention layout in Section 4
claim: The token-copy quantity bounds remote all-to-all traffic, with equality requiring zero local copies.
analysis: With two devices, one expert each and top-\(k\) routing with \(k=2\), each token makes one local and one remote copy. The universal bound \(2\) is valid; the tight remote count for that fixed layout is \(1\). Under unrestricted per-token expert routing, the fixed-layout maximum is \(\sum_i n_i\min(k,N_e-m_i)/\sum_i n_i\). A source device holding no experts can attain the general bound.
result: This is a quantifier clarification, not a counterexample to the original inequality or the concrete Mozart attention-source layout. It must not be counted as a second disproved theorem.
assumptions: The finding concerns the stated source version and mathematical or released-code scope.
problems.impact_rationale: No error is established in this scoped claim; the stated qualification is compatible with the source.
problems.existing_correction_status: The latest paper retains a valid general upper bound. The fixed-layout distinction is explanatory counterevidence, not an author correction or a current error.

impact_rationale: The supported findings concern local equations, released implementation details, reporting or bounded interpretation. No demonstrated failure of the paper's central result meets the stricter Major threshold.
